quickSummary: An ionic bond forms via complete electron transfer between an electropositive cation and electronegative anion. The Born-Haber thermodynamic cycle applies Hess's law to determine Lattice Enthalpy: Δ_f H° = Δ_sub H + (1/2)Δ_bond H + Δ_i H + Δ_eg H + U.
summary: Master ionic bonding energetics, Born-Haber cycle calculations, and the Born-Landé lattice enthalpy relationship.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.1 The Born-Haber Thermodynamic Cycle
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.1 The Born-Haber Thermodynamic Cycle

summaryBox.title: Born-Haber Cycle
summaryBox.takeaway: Δ_f H° = Δ_sub H + 1/2 Δ_bond H + Δ_i H + Δ_eg H + U. Lattice enthalpy U is always exothermic (U < 0).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
BORN-HABER THERMODYNAMIC CYCLE (NaCl)
                      
   Na(s) + 1/2 Cl₂(g) ───[Δ_f H° = -411 kJ/mol]───► NaCl(s)
     │         │                                        ▲
  [Δ_sub H] [1/2 Δ_bond H]                              │
     ▼         ▼                                        │
   Na(g)     Cl(g)                                      │ [U (Lattice Energy)]
     │         │                                        │
   [Δ_i H]   [Δ_eg H]                                   │
     ▼         ▼                                        │
   Na⁺(g)  +  Cl⁻(g) ───────────────────────────────────┘
conceptBreakdown.content:
According to Hess's Law of Constant Heat Summation, the standard enthalpy of formation ($\Delta_f H^\circ$) of an ionic solid is:

$$\mathbf{\Delta_f H^\circ = \Delta_{\text{sub}} H + \frac{1}{2} \Delta_{\text{bond}} H + \Delta_i H + \Delta_{\text{eg}} H + U}$$

• $\Delta_{\text{sub}} H$: Sublimation enthalpy of metal ($\text{Na}(s) \rightarrow \text{Na}(g) > 0$)
• $\Delta_{\text{bond}} H$: Dissociation enthalpy of halogen gas ($\text{Cl}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{Cl}(g) > 0$)
• $\Delta_i H$: Ionization enthalpy of metal ($\text{Na}(g) \rightarrow \text{Na}^+(g) + e^- > 0$)
• $\Delta_{\text{eg}} H$: Electron gain enthalpy of non-metal ($\text{Cl}(g) + e^- \rightarrow \text{Cl}^-(g) < 0$)
• $U$: Lattice Enthalpy of ionic crystal ($\text{Na}^+(g) + \text{Cl}^-(g) \rightarrow \text{NaCl}(s) < 0$)

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.2 Factors Governing Lattice Enthalpy (U)
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.2 Factors Governing Lattice Enthalpy (U)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Lattice enthalpy is the energy released when $1\text{ mole}$ of an ionic crystal lattice is formed from its constituent gaseous ions (Born-Landé Equation):

$$\mathbf{U \propto -\frac{z^+ \cdot z^-}{r_+ + r^-}}$$

1. **Magnitude of Ionic Charges ($z^+, z^-$)**: $U$ increases directly with ionic charges ($U_{\text{MgO}} \approx 4 \times U_{\text{NaCl}}$ because $z^+ z^- = 4$ for $\text{MgO}$ vs $1$ for $\text{NaCl}$).
2. **Inter-ionic Distance ($r_+ + r^-$)**: $U$ increases as ionic radii decrease ($U_{\text{LiF}} > U_{\text{NaCl}} > U_{\text{KBr}}$).

quickRevision: Born-Haber formula: Δ_f H° = Δ_sub H + Δ_i H + 1/2 Δ_bond H + Δ_eg H + U.
MgO lattice energy is ~4× higher than NaCl due to charge multiplication (2×2=4).
High lattice energy stabilizes ionic crystals and elevates melting points.
